decisions: Add one raw-only staging bucket owned by the exact native-approved recording object, source object, track state and structural unit. Coalesce only consecutive data with the same ownership tuple. A different track or unit flushes the old bucket before accepting new bytes; no cross-track reordering, init mixing or mutation of an already queued/in-flight payload.

The bucket holds at most128KiB owned bytes. Copy every accepted caller slice synchronously during the existing successful append wrapper; never retain caller memory for a later timer. Do not await disk, ACK or timers in SourceBuffer.appendBuffer. Preserve its return values and exceptions.

Flush at128KiB or250ms from the bucket's first byte, never sliding the deadline on arrivals. Recheck expired deadlines on each append. Timers cannot guarantee hard real time while JavaScript is suspended; record this limitation and validate actual hidden-receiver latency. Source/account/page/owner invalidation cannot let an old timer enqueue into a successor.

On encoded_raw_init: flush older staged bytes first, then enqueue the unchanged exact init request, then later data. Native initialization remains authoritative and once per structural unit, including harmless changed padding. A new init never bypasses pending old-byte ACKs.

The first video successor rawFirstUnitEnd hint forces all prior staged data out and sends that hint-bearing data through the existing immediate path without added staging delay. Its init must already precede it in the queue. Preserve exact boundary offset, first-chunk placement, once-only hint, native receive-time anchor and15second startup deadline. Never attach the hint to older pooled bytes or refresh its time on retry.

Assign appendIndex only when a logical append is sealed/enqueued. Existing128KiB chunk division, finalChunk and identical immediate retry semantics remain unchanged. SourceBuffer call boundaries are not native structural evidence; original byte order and init offsets are. Large offered data at or above the staging target uses the existing bounded large-append path after flushing the bucket, avoiding an increase to128 Promise tasks for a16MiB append.

Count staging, queued and in-flight bytes exactly once under the existing64MiB budget. Transfer that reservation on flush rather than double-counting it; release once after ACK/failure. Keep512 pending-task and existing append/IPC limits. Allocation/budget failure still stops explicitly; no silent eviction or success after dropped data.

Normal explicit stop seals the owned bucket synchronously before accepting=false/disarm and before finish captures its queue, then drains the unchanged serial queue before encoded_finish. The existing accepted prefix must also drain after a local queue-cap stop. Transport/native rejection must not send new staged bytes after terminal rejection; release them and preserve an interrupted result. Page invalidation/closed transport may prevent final delivery and is never claimed lossless. Clear timers exactly once on finish/cleanup/cancel; no stale completion may flush into another recording.

Do not reduce durable syncs, throttle the native job journal, enlarge limits, force codecs, drop frames or introduce parallel A/V IPC in this batch. Any later native performance change needs its own evidence and contract.

lifecycleProtocol.preapproval: No staging bucket or task/byte reservation exists before encoded_begin ACK.nativeApproved. Raw framers remain metadata-only until the existing post-ACK arm; no preapproval media is retained, and failed/delayed begin or cancel-before-ACK cannot create a bucket.
lifecycleProtocol.capacity: A newly created bucket reserves exactly one of the existing512 pending slots plus its actual owned-byte budget. Growing it reserves only extra bytes. Flushing transfers its already-reserved slot/bytes to one serial work item without reacquiring a slot or double-counting. This avoids a full-queue failure recursively preventing already accepted staged bytes from being drained. Allocation failure rolls back only the new uncommitted reservation before terminal failure. Init requests continue to reserve independent slots.
lifecycleProtocol.seal: Seal detaches the exact bucket from current first and clears its exact timer before queue installation. It cannot re-enter failure through a second capacity check: capacity was already reserved. The sealed payload is immutable and belongs to one queue item; finally releases its slot/bytes exactly once. A stale timer checks bucket identity and recording ownership and cannot seal another bucket or rearm itself.
lifecycleProtocol.stopAndFailure: Normal stop and local queue-cap failure first prevent new producer admission with an explicit draining/latching state, synchronously seal the accepted bucket, then set the final accepting=false/disarm state and capture the serial drain promise. A reentrant finish/failure call observes the latch and cannot double-seal or overwrite the first terminal reason. Existing finish Promise remains single-flight. Native/transport rejection instead marks terminal before cleanup so unsent bytes cannot be issued after rejection; this must stay interrupted and is not represented as a lossless drain.
lifecycleProtocol.pageAndCancel: pagehide/cancel/cleanup cancels the exact staging timer. If the original recording transport/epoch still permits the existing stop path, its accepted bucket is sealed there once; otherwise cleanup releases only that obsolete bucket and never forwards it to a new document. No new pagehide guarantee or synthetic wall-time anchor. Raw continuation remains disabled, and cancelled exact arm IDs remain authoritative.
